precepts.text: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein. He that worketh mischief, it shall fall upon him, and he shall not know whence it cometh, because his pride hath deceived him. Mockery and reproach are from the proud; but vengeance, as a lion, shall lie in wait for them. They that rejoice at the fall of the righteous shall be taken in the snare, and anguish shall consume them before they die. They thought evil against us, but the Lord saw it for good. Jacob is going to win in the end.
precepts.point: In closing: there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt. That is Esau. The way Esau treated us is going to be to his own detriment.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that setteth a trap shall be taken therein.” The proud digged pits for us, and they will fall in them. They thought evil against us, but the Lord saw it for good. Jacob is going to win in the end.

“He that worketh mischief, it shall fall upon him, and he shall not know whence it cometh.” That is what they do: they work mischief and call it law. And he is not going to know where it came from, because his pride has deceived him.

“Mockery and reproach are from the proud”. That is all they do: they accuse us, falsely accuse us, and mock us. “but vengeance, as a lion, shall lie in wait for them.” That lion is the one in Jeremiah 4:7.

“They that rejoice at the fall of the righteous shall be taken in the snare; and anguish shall consume them before they die.” Remember when they said raze it, raze it to the ground? The Lord has not forgotten. They will be taken in the snare. It does not pay to be wicked, and it does not pay to follow after your oppressor, because in the end they are going to be destroyed.

precepts.text: An officer tied it back to the fire: the furnace proveth the potter's vessels, so the trial of man is in his reasoning. When the Lord turns up the heat, he is trying your heart, and your reasoning gets revealed. You lost the job, and now you want to pick up a job on the Sabbath: your reasoning is off; covetousness is revealed. You get checked and you argue and have strife: ego is revealed. As the fire goes up in your life, different spirits rise to the top like metal in the melt. He is dealing with you as a son; are you going to respect him as a father? That is why it says take it cheerfully: you are getting purged as he tries your reasoning, and you get to show forth whether everything you have been hearing is actually being learned and applied.
precepts.point: For what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? As a father you have to correct your son, because if you do not correct him, you do not love him; and as a father you want to see your son do better than you. It is the same in the truth: the heads of the school are fathers over the congregation and treat you as sons, and our leadership are fathers over us; we get chastised just as much as you do, if not more. But that is out of love. And some will turn their back to that and take their ball and go home.
precepts.why:
“For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth.” That correction, that chastisement, is the Lord trying your heart, seeing what your heart is made out of. Sirach ties it back to the fire: “The furnace proveth the potter’s vessels; so the trial of man is in his reasoning.”

The furnace proves the potter’s vessel, but what is the Lord proving? A man’s reasoning. When the Lord turns up the heat on your behind, he is going to try your heart. You have a couple of flat tires, you lost a job, and now you want to pick up a job on the Sabbath. Your reasoning is off, and now it is revealed: covetous. You can’t deal with your lowest state. Or you get checked, maybe it wasn’t exactly your fault, and you don’t take the low; you argue, you have strife. That is ego, and the fire revealed your thoughts.

When the potter melts the metal, each metal has a different temperature to melt and be purged. So as the fire goes up in your life, different spirits are going to come out and rise to the top. He is trying your reasoning. Are you going to deal with it or not? He is dealing with you as a son; are you going to respect him as a father?

That is why you take it cheerfully: you are getting purged as he tries your reasoning, and you get to show forth your understanding, whether everything you have been hearing is actually being learned and applied. And the trial shows other things too. Many like to suffer in silence, and the Lord is showing you your communication is weak. “Then they that feared the Lord spake often one to another.” When you are going through things, lean on the brothers; call and say I am struggling in this area. Out of pride we suffer in silence, get offended with everybody, and find ourselves out the door.

If he did not love us, he would cut us off, as he cut off Esau, whom he hates. You are supposed to go through it. Three flat tires? You have one more tire than you deserve. A whole kingdom is waiting on us, the world turned right side up, and we have to push through it manfully, together, or not at all.

precepts.text: As a nail sticketh fast between the joinings of the stones, so doth sin stick close between buying and selling. When you are dealing in business with a sinner, the balances will be offset: he will not take a five percent interest, he wants one hundred or two hundred percent.
precepts.point: If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold. They did not just kill the one man that hurt Lamech; they wiped out that whole lineage. That is how Esau gets down; remember who their desire was to.
precepts.why:
“As a nail sticketh fast between the joinings of the stones; so doth sin stick close between buying and selling.” When you are dealing in business with a sinner, the balances will be offset, because he always takes the favor, exceedingly. He will not take a five percent interest; he wants a hundred or two hundred percent.

That opens up Jabal, “the father of such as dwell in tents, and of such as have cattle.” It sounds harmless, but this is the seed of Cain in Cain's city. Jabal was dealing in tents and cattle with pricing and unrighteousness, buying and selling with sin stuck fast in between.

What Cain's seed did in the city of Enoch is what sinners do in business today. There is no new thing under the sun.

precepts.text: Observe the time when you are among the indiscreet.
precepts.point: The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his way, but the folly of fools is deceit. Fools make a mock at sin, but among the righteous there is favor.
precepts.why:
“Go from the presence of a foolish man, when thou perceivest not in him the lips of knowledge.” This is why the scripture says: “If thou be among the indiscreet, observe the time; but be continually among men of understanding.”

When you are among the indiscreet, observe the time; when you perceive there are no lips of knowledge in a man, go from his presence and be continually among men of understanding.

points: Sin sticks close between buying and selling: sin is never far from business, and if it is not built on the scriptures it is not of God.
Watch a three-hour debate and you will hear four or five scriptures at most; the rest is scholars, because the book does not belong to them and the spirit in them hates it.
The discourse of fools is irksome: listen to one plus one plus one is one for three hours and you will lose your mind.

Their sport is in the wantonness of sin: the premise of the whole doctrine is that only a being with two essences, fully God and fully man, can keep the commandments, so a man does not have to; that is what all the big words boil down to.
If thou be among the indiscreet, observe the time; but be continually among men of understanding. Be around likeminded people that are on the same healing journey.

note.label: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

points: Whoso discovereth secrets loseth his credit, and shall never find friend to his mind. You will instantly lose credit, because now everybody knows he's a blabbermouth. That's why it makes it difficult for that person to make friends: they lack self-control.

Love thy friend, and be faithful unto him: faithful meaning when he's there with you and when he's not there with you. But if thou bewrayest his secrets, follow no more after him. You might as well let that person go, cuz to win them back again is damn near impossible.
As one that letteth a bird go out of his hand, so hast thou let thy neighbour go. The moment you let that bird out of your hand, the bird gone. Same as that friend whose secrets you told.

As for a wound, it may be bound up; and after reviling there may be reconcilement. How many of y'all fought your friends when you was young? Had a black eye and everything, and guess what? You cool, you let it go. But he that bewrayeth secrets is without hope. Bewray secrets and see what happens. Scripture says, let him go.

Many have sinned for a small matter, and he that seeketh for abundance will turn his eyes away. Ten grand for a job promised in two months and still not done two years later is a small matter that became sin, because you did not live by your word.

points: Unless a man hold himself diligently in the fear of the Lord, his house shall soon be overthrown. Diligent means steady, earnest, painstaking effort. Idleness teaches much evil, so stay busy and stay in the Bible, where the stories teach you the do's and don'ts, like Joseph who ran.
